subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a supported per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding this config surface changes public configuration and provider/session routing semantics, which requires maintainer intent before automation should create or reshape a fix.

options.title: Sponsor additive per-agent config
options.body: Approve the direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` now and defer broader compaction/contextPruning merge semantics to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline the config expansion and close or redirect the open implementation PRs, leaving users with global defaults or separate instances.

recommendation.title: Sponsor additive per-agent config
recommendation.body: Approve the direction, require deep-merge semantics plus docs/tests/upgrade proof, and use the open PR as the repair or replacement path.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history on agent config, provider/auth routing, and agent-scope helpers where this contract would land.
